response.sql: SELECT t.account_id, a.frequency, AVG(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount WHEN t.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount END) AS avg_signed_amount, AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id WHERE t.amount > 2400 GROUP BY t.account_id, a.frequency ORDER BY avg_balance DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: A large transaction is one with amount strictly greater than 2400 (not >= 2400).

The average balance covers all large transactions, including those of other types such as VYBER. Only the signed-amount average ignores other types, because AVG skips the NULLs the CASE produces for them.
Ties at the 10th place are cut arbitrarily by LIMIT 10.

alternatives.interpretation: Large means amount >= 2400 (the cutoff value itself counts).
alternatives.sql: SELECT t.account_id, a.frequency, AVG(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount WHEN t.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount END) AS avg_signed_amount, AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id WHERE t.amount >= 2400 GROUP BY t.account_id, a.frequency ORDER BY avg_balance DESC LIMIT 10

alternatives.interpretation: Other types are dropped entirely, so both averages use only PRIJEM and VYDAJ large transactions.
